## Delegation (Claude Code)

This section is rendered by the AgentKit plugin ( `{{PLUGIN_URL}}` ). Change the rules there, then re-run `init.sh`; repo-specific rules go outside the markers.

AGENTS.md's Autonomy section, done with Claude Code's tools. The plugin's `factory` skill is the loop; verify command of this repo: `{{VERIFY}}`.

- Start follow-up tickets yourself with the Agent tool, in the background, not as prompts for {{OWNER_NAME}} to paste into new sessions. Use Opus
  for large milestones and Sonnet for small, well-specified ones. Give the
  agent the ticket, its branch, worktree and port; when it reports back, review its result ( the ticket's checks, `{{VERIFY}}` ) before merging.
- Set each agent's reasoning effort explicitly ( the Agent tool's `effort` ): `high` for builders by default,
  `xhigh` for foundations that later work builds on ( a new API, coordinate maths ), `medium` for small mechanical
  tickets on Sonnet. A plan may set it per milestone; that wins. An orchestrating
  session itself runs at `high` and raises it only for a real judgement call ( reviewing an API, a milestone that missed its target ).
- Before starting one, check ListAgents: don't duplicate a session {{OWNER_NAME}} already opened. A peer session's transcript is
  `~/.claude/projects/{{TRANSCRIPT_DIR}}/<session id>.jsonl` ( read-only ): read its end to tell finished from waiting for an answer.
- Subagent prompts must say "assume and record under **Assumptions** in the ticket, don't ask" ( AGENTS.md, Autonomy: assumptions over questions ); reports to {{OWNER_NAME}} over several tickets are a bullet list, one bullet per ticket with the number, the title and one sentence on what the ticket is, never two tickets in one paragraph ( AGENTS.md, Autonomy ); read each builder's assumptions in review and list them in your report to {{OWNER_NAME}}.
- A builder prompt for a visible change must ask for the context captures ( AGENTS.md, Autonomy: belongs-there acceptance ) and name the neighbours to compare with; review against them, not against the old flaw.
- Keep the orchestration state outside the conversation, in `STATE.md` ( AGENTS.md, Autonomy ): rewrite it at every hand-back, spawn and owner decision. A fresh session reads it first, then `board.sh state` ( a draft of the sheet from the board ). The conversation may be compacted at any time; everything else lives in the tickets and on the branches.
- Builder prompts carry the heartbeat ( AGENTS.md, Autonomy ): commit WIP or post a one-line progress note at least every 30 minutes; say in one line what you wait on and for how long instead of waiting silently; never wait more than 20 minutes on a lock or another agent without reporting.
- Watchdog: every 30 minutes run the plugin's `scripts/board.sh stale` and compare it with the `Last progress` column of `STATE.md`. No progress for 45 minutes: one ping ( SendMessage ) with a precise next step. No progress 20 minutes after the ping: stop the agent ( TaskStop ), note its state in `STATE.md`, and start a successor on the same worktree from the state sheet. Never wait on an agent for more than an hour; {{OWNER_NAME}} must not be the one who notices.
- Never ask {{OWNER_NAME}} to start a new session: compaction is automatic and `STATE.md` plus the board make it lossless, so keep going. Per batch of tickets, start one long-lived **shift lead** ( an orchestrator subagent ) that reads `STATE.md`, starts and reviews the builders, merges and reports only decisions and short summaries; when its context grows large it rewrites `STATE.md` and reports, and you start the next one. The root session stays thin.
- Wait with Monitor ( the plugin's `scripts/watch.sh`, a script that prints a line per change: a card moving, a transcript going quiet ), never by polling in a loop. A Monitor expires; re-arm it when it does.
- Budget: the usage limit is a token budget per 5-hour window shared by every agent. Run at most six builders at once ( `agentsMax` ), and only as many as the machine allows; Sonnet `medium` for mechanical tickets without geometry ( Sonnet never generates 3D geometry ), Opus `high` for milestones, judgement and all geometry; the tier above Opus only when {{OWNER_NAME}} asks for it by name or after several rejected revisions on Opus, and then only for the form-critical steps of the ticket ( cascade: top tier, then Opus, then Sonnet, one after another ); `agentsMax` is a hard cap that counts every subagent; ask {{OWNER_NAME}} for the weekly usage before a batch and plan against it ( above 70 %: two builders at most; above 85 %: wind down, nothing new without a yes ); quick verify by default, full verify only for sky, terrain or post-processing; capture sets only where the acceptance names them. The orchestrator's own share is small; keep it on the strongest model.
- Capacity ( AGENTS.md, Autonomy ): run the plugin's `scripts/capacity.sh --json` before every spawn and every 30 minutes with the watchdog; spawn only while its `agents` is above the number running; when `free_headless` is 0, pause browser work, not agents. {{OWNER_NAME}}'s own use comes first: headroom while active, the full machine when idle, `agentsMax` + 2 when AFK; when {{OWNER_NAME}} says the machine is slow, halve the recommendation until told otherwise. Write the result into `STATE.md` ( Limits ).
- Two phases per ticket: an Opus builder builds and stops at a short handover; a Sonnet `medium` finisher runs the full verify, captures, ticket, merge ( under `scripts/mergelock.sh` ); only your deployer agent deploys: after a batch's merges, start one on the cheapest model ( never two at once ) that, under `scripts/mergelock.sh`, verifies the integration tip, builds, runs the gated deploy script with read-back and returns one line ( sha, entry file, read-back ); you decide when and write that line into `STATE.md` ( AGENTS.md, Branches ). Builders read big files by grep and line range, never whole; no new builder in the last hour of a usage window.
- Subagents pause when the account's usage window is exhausted ( HTTP 429 ): their state is on their branch. Resume each with SendMessage once the window has reset; do not restart them.
- Subagents end with the session that started them: for work that must outlive it, start a separate session.
